purpose: A richer title-analysis envelope containing fingerprint attributes plus separate facts, advisories, contexts, evaluations, and reception.

terminology.fingerprint: Descriptive experience, content, world, and form attributes. Quality evaluations and reception are separate outputs of title analysis.
terminology.attribute_id: Stable group.key identifier; display labels and aliases do not create additional dimensions.
terminology.core_candidate: Eligible for evaluation as a general-similarity feature; inclusion and weight are not yet decided.
terminology.targeted_only: Available for targeted retrieval and filters; not automatically a general-similarity feature.

source_notes: TODO.md: subgenre descriptions through holiday + audience

output_contract.definition_file: definition.json contains the vocabulary, definitions, measurement rubrics, migration examples, and retrieval policies.
output_contract.instance_schema: schema.json defines a single title-analysis document; example-matrix.json demonstrates that document shape.
output_contract.fingerprint_path: analyses[].fingerprint contains descriptive groups. The evaluations registry group is emitted at analyses[].evaluations, outside the fingerprint.
output_contract.vocabulary_not_checklist: The registry is a broad vocabulary, not a requirement to generate hundreds of scores for every title. Record coverage and assess only traits supported by the available evidence.
output_contract.generation_strategy: Evaluate a stable core candidate set, retrieve relevant long-tail concepts, and explicitly assess requested exclusion topics. Do not silently convert unselected concepts to absence.
output_contract.cost_and_reliability: Measure generation cost, repeat-run stability, human agreement, and evidence coverage before adding any trait to the required production core.
output_contract.compatibility: This draft does not change V1 storage, attribute order, generated scores, UI families, or production retrieval. Migrating compound fields requires reassessment rather than copying one value into every split field.

scoring_contract.intermediate_values: Integers between anchors interpolate within the same rubric. Do not imply measured precision beyond evidence.

statuses.assessed: Evidence supports a value, including zero.
statuses.unknown: Assessment attempted but evidence is insufficient or conflicting; value must be null.
statuses.not_applicable: The concept does not apply to this work or scope; value must be null.
statuses.not_assessed: No assessment was attempted; value must be null.

scoring_contract.omission: An omitted field is not assessed, never zero, false, or verified absent.
scoring_contract.confidence: Ordinal editorial assessment of evidence support, not a calibrated probability. Assessed values require low, medium, or high plus evidence references.
scoring_contract.scope: Every assessment belongs to an explicit movie, whole-show, season, or episode scope with an as-of date and coverage statement.

intensity.10: Exceptionally strong or pervasive in the defined scope.

centrality.10: Defining focus; removing it fundamentally changes the work.

membership.0: Does not use the genre conventions.

prominence.8: Prominent across much of the scope.

quality.10: Exceptional execution. Absence is not a zero-quality score.

suitability.0: Very poor fit under the stated assumptions.
suitability.10: Exceptionally strong fit. Not a universal audience verdict.

separate_dimensions: Genre membership is not subject presence.
Release era is not setting era.
Production origin is not depicted culture or influence.
Intended audience is not age suitability.
Aesthetic appearance does not establish production technique.
scoring_contract.advisory_absence: An absent advisory requires sufficient coverage of the relevant scope and version. Do not turn synopsis silence into absence.
scoring_contract.series_policy: Movie scopes mark series traits not_applicable or omit them. Whole-show assessments name covered seasons/episodes. Compare scoped assessments for change over time; never encode viewer lost-interest as an intrinsic trait.

dream_sequences.definition: Use of dreams or hallucinations as presented sequences.

observational_mode.definition: Attention to behavior and environments without strong explanatory or plot intervention.

slice_of_life.definition: Emphasis on ordinary experience rather than extraordinary plot escalation.

exposition_load.definition: Amount of explanatory information the viewer must absorb.

information_withholding.definition: Deliberate delay in supplying information needed to understand events.

educational_intent.definition: Deliberate presentation of factual knowledge for learning.

formal_challenge.definition: Departure from familiar formal conventions that demands adaptation.

homage.definition: Recognizable tributes and references to other works.

pastiche.definition: Imitation or combination of recognizable artistic styles.

personal.definition: Consequences for an individual's life, identity, or goals.

relationship.definition: Consequences for a central relationship or small social unit.

community.definition: Consequences for a locality or community.

societal.definition: Consequences for institutions, a society, or civilization.

planetary.definition: Consequences extending to a planet or humanity as a whole.

cosmic.definition: Consequences extending beyond planetary life to cosmic reality.

urgency.definition: Time pressure on consequential decisions or events.

density.definition: Amount of spoken dialogue relative to the work's running time.

dependence.definition: Importance of understanding dialogue to follow the work.

overlap.definition: Use of simultaneous or overlapping speech.

naturalistic_delivery.definition: Conversational delivery resembling spontaneous everyday speech.

theatrical_delivery.definition: Heightened, rhetorical, or explicitly performative speech.

multilingual_exchange.definition: Use of multiple languages within the work; factual languages are catalog data.

cyberpunk.definition: High technology combined with alienation, social stratification, or countercultural urban imagery.

steampunk.definition: Retro-industrial speculative imagery drawing on steam-age technology.

gothic.definition: Ominous, decaying, or romantically macabre visual atmosphere.

noir.definition: Shadowed, morally uneasy visual and atmospheric treatment, independently of crime plotting.

retro.definition: Deliberately retrospective visual or sonic styling; not merely an older release.

minimalism.definition: Reduction of visual, sonic, or formal elements.

stylization.definition: Departure from naturalistic presentation through a distinctive audiovisual treatment.

surrealism.definition: Dreamlike or illogical relationships in presented images and events.

psychedelia.definition: Hallucinatory, distorted, or perceptually altered sensory treatment.

grotesquerie.definition: Emphasis on distorted, repulsive, or biologically unsettling forms.

camp.definition: Theatrical excess and conspicuous artifice with an invitation to enjoy that excess.

ironic_distance.definition: Presentation that invites distance from its apparent surface meaning.

intimacy.definition: Presentation fostering closeness to characters' private experience.

spectacle.definition: Emphasis on impressive scale, effects, and set pieces.

immersion.definition: Strength of the sensory sense of inhabiting the work's world.

muted_palette.definition: Use of restrained or desaturated colors.

neon_palette.definition: Use of luminous, neon-like color accents.

restricted_palette.definition: Use of a narrow or monochromatic color range.

warm_color.definition: Prominence of warm hues and lighting.

cool_color.definition: Prominence of cool hues and lighting.

low_key_lighting.definition: Predominance of dark lighting with selective illumination.

high_key_lighting.definition: Predominance of bright, evenly illuminated scenes.

high_contrast.definition: Strong contrast between light and dark regions.

long_takes.definition: Prominence of extended shots without cuts; method of capture is irrelevant.

handheld_motion.definition: Prominence of visibly handheld or unstable camera movement.

aerial_viewpoints.definition: Prominence of aerial views, independently of capture technology.

closeups.definition: Prominence of tight framing on faces or details.

practical_effects.definition: Prominence of physical on-set effects; do not infer exact production method from appearance alone.

digital_effects.definition: Prominence of digitally produced or altered imagery.

costume_emphasis.definition: Expressive prominence of clothing and costume design.

production_design_detail.definition: Density of expressive detail in constructed environments and props.

split_screen.definition: Prominence of simultaneous images in separate screen regions.

aspect_ratio_changes.definition: Expressive use of changes in frame proportions.

grain_texture.definition: Visible grain-like image texture, independently of capture medium.

distressed_texture.definition: Deliberate wear, damage, or degraded-image treatment.

martial_arts_choreography.definition: Combat organized around recognizable or stylized martial arts movement.

grappling.definition: Combat involving holds, clinches, throws, or ground fighting.

gun_fu.definition: Highly stylized choreography combining firearms and close-quarters movement.

blade_combat.definition: Combat involving swords, knives, or similar blades.

superpowered_combat.definition: Combat involving abilities beyond ordinary human capacities.

large_battles.definition: Combat involving many participants or military-scale engagement.

environmental_choreography.definition: Creative use of surroundings and objects in action.

gritty_combat.definition: Combat presented as physically punishing, messy, and effortful.

stylized_violence.definition: Violence presented through conspicuously aestheticized movement or imagery.

realistic_violence.definition: Violence presented with plausible physical consequences and vulnerability.

possession.definition: Possession of a person by a supernatural entity matters to the horror.

body_horror.definition: Transformation, violation, or instability of the body matters to the horror.

folk_horror.definition: Folk belief, ritual, landscape, or insular tradition matters to the horror.

cosmic_horror.definition: Human insignificance before incomprehensible forces matters to the horror.

psychological_horror.definition: Perception, mental distress, or internal instability drives the horror.

design_prominence.definition: Expressive prominence of non-musical sound design; not a quality judgment.

ambient_soundscapes.definition: Use of environmental sound to create atmosphere.

silence.definition: Expressive use of silence or near silence.

sparse_score.definition: Use of little or no non-diegetic score.

audio_startles.definition: Abrupt sound events intended to startle.

audio_self_reference.definition: Sound that acknowledges or plays with the work's representational frame.

music_dependence.definition: Importance of music to emotional or narrative understanding.

nonmusical_sound_dependence.definition: Importance of non-musical sound to emotional or narrative understanding.

diegetic_music.definition: Prominence of music audible within the story world.

preexisting_recordings.definition: Prominence of preexisting recorded songs or pieces placed in the soundtrack.

live_performance.definition: Prominence of scenes depicting musical performance.

musical_numbers.definition: Prominence of song or dance sequences functioning as narrative expression.

orchestral.definition: Orchestral music in the audible soundtrack.

electronic.definition: Electronic music in the audible soundtrack.

classical.definition: Classical traditions in the audible soundtrack; can coexist with orchestral instrumentation.

hip_hop.definition: Hip-hop or rap in the audible soundtrack.

folk.definition: Folk traditions in the audible soundtrack; name specific traditions in cultural annotations.

conflict_resolution.definition: Extent to which central dramatic conflicts receive an outcome; independent of happiness.

interpretive_openness.definition: Extent to which the ending permits multiple interpretations.

emotional_closure.definition: Extent of emotional completion or release at the ending.

happiness.definition: Positive emotional outcome for focal characters at the ending.

tragedy.definition: Loss, defeat, or suffering defining the ending.

bittersweetness.definition: Intertwined positive and painful outcomes at the ending.

twist_impact.definition: Extent to which the ending reframes prior understanding.

cliffhanger.definition: Extent to which the ending suspends an urgent unresolved event.

sequel_dependence.definition: Extent to which another installment is needed to resolve central conflicts.

cyclical_return.definition: Extent to which the ending returns to or repeats the initial situation.

episodic_independence.definition: Extent to which episodes provide independently understandable stories.

serialized_dependence.definition: Extent to which episodes rely on ongoing arcs and prior episodes.

anthology_independence.definition: Extent to which episodes or seasons form distinct stories with separate continuity.

episode_cliffhangers.definition: Strength of suspended outcomes at episode boundaries.

bottle_episode_pattern.definition: Prominence of episodes deliberately limited in location or cast.

cold_open_hooks.definition: Prominence of openings designed to generate curiosity before titles or setup.

formula_repetition.definition: Recurrence of substantially similar plot patterns across episodes.

conceptual_renewal.definition: Introduction of new situations, ideas, or narrative directions across episodes.

attention.definition: Sustained concentration needed to follow the work.

visual_dependence.definition: Importance of watching the image to understand events; distinct from spectacle.

auditory_dependence.definition: Importance of hearing sound to follow events; accessibility version may alter this.

sensory_intensity.definition: Strength and density of audiovisual stimulation.

franchise_knowledge.definition: Need for familiarity with other installments to understand this work.

genre_knowledge.definition: Need for familiarity with genre conventions to understand this work.

historical_knowledge.definition: Need for historical background not explained in the work.

cultural_knowledge.definition: Need for cultural background not explained in the work.

onscreen_reading.definition: Importance of reading text embedded in the image; subtitle demand is derived separately per viewer and offer.

background_viewing.definition: Ease of following the work with intermittent attention; not inferred from pace alone.

drop_in_viewing.definition: Ease of joining after the start without significant confusion.

standalone_viewing.definition: Ease of understanding this work without other franchise installments.

discussion.definition: Scope for discussion of ideas, characters, or interpretation after viewing.

theorizing.definition: Scope for speculation about concealed information or unresolved mysteries.

repeat_discovery.definition: Scope for discovering additional details or interpretations on another viewing; distinct from personal desire to rewatch.

direction.definition: Assessment of coherence and execution of the creative vision.

acting.definition: Assessment of performance execution, not the presence of live-action performers.

dialogue.definition: Assessment of dialogue writing as a component of writing.

characterization.definition: Assessment of nuance and development in character writing.

narrative_cohesion.definition: Assessment of causal, structural, and thematic coherence.

cinematography.definition: Assessment of visual storytelling and photographic execution.

editing.definition: Assessment of shot assembly, rhythm, and transitions.

original_score.definition: Assessment of original musical composition, when present.

sound_design.definition: Assessment of the execution of non-musical sound.

related_attributes.weighting: Do not sum as independent evidence without evaluating correlation.
A horror genre match does not establish matching fear intensity.
Do not infer any one from either of the others.
Broad and specific matches share a feature budget.
Do not independently double count the broad and specific match.
Keep direction-specific retrieval without multiplying the broad mechanism contribution.
Normalize within the genre group; no additive hierarchy bonus.

advisory_topics.violence: Physical violence or intentional bodily harm.
advisory_topics.gore: Graphic wounds, blood, or bodily destruction.
advisory_topics.nudity: Depicted nudity, independently of sexual activity.
advisory_topics.substance_use: Use of intoxicating or addictive substances.
advisory_topics.disturbing_imagery: Imagery likely to be upsetting through its content rather than plot stakes alone.
advisory_topics.child_endangerment: Threatened or actual harm to a child.
advisory_topics.animal_harm: Threatened or actual injury, cruelty, or death affecting an animal.
advisory_topics.self_harm: Intentional self-injury, separately from suicidal behavior.
advisory_topics.suicide: Suicidal ideation, attempts, or death by suicide.
advisory_topics.sexual_violence: Sexual assault, coercive sexual conduct, or threats of such conduct.
advisory_topics.domestic_abuse: Abuse within intimate or domestic relationships.
advisory_topics.police_brutality: Abusive force or treatment by police.
advisory_topics.torture: Deliberate infliction of severe suffering on a captive or controlled person.
advisory_topics.pregnancy_loss: Miscarriage, stillbirth, or other loss of a pregnancy.
advisory_topics.discrimination: Discriminatory abuse or exclusion; identify its specific target in notes.
advisory_topics.flashing_imagery: Flashing or strobing imagery; an editorial observation is not a technical accessibility certification.

world_contexts.purpose: Separate reality layers and their settings rather than conflating apparent era with actual chronology.
world_contexts.place_policy: Use controlled place identifiers when established; do not infer setting from production country or filming location.

cultural_contexts.policy: Use named controlled concepts, not one-dimensional national-character scores. Interpretations require attribution and never establish explicit representation.

seasonal_contexts.policy: Christmas taking place in the story, Christmas as a major theme, and suitability for Christmas viewing are distinct. Calendar and hemisphere qualify seasonal labels.

format.policy: These are sourced facts. Limited-series design is separate from current renewal/cancellation status. Anime tradition is separate from animation technique.

representation_annotations.policy: Only explicit_text or attributed_source establishes a represented identity. Allegory and critical interpretations belong in cultural_contexts. Specific racial, ethnic, religious, gender, and disability identities use sourced annotations rather than an aggregate diversity score.

temporal_segments.purpose: Optional opening, middle, and ending assessments preserve emotional and pacing changes hidden by whole-work averages.
temporal_segments.policy: Segment positions use fractions of the assessed scope. Distinguish within-work changes from season-to-season changes.

audience_contexts.policy: Require age bounds where age suitability is claimed, plus language, familiarity, and content tolerances when relevant. Familiar comfort and rewatch desire depend on the viewer. Do not invent universal kids, teen, or date-night scores.

reception.purpose: Attributed observations and interpretations outside descriptive fingerprint similarity.
reception.policy: Separate measured facts, attributed judgments, and hypotheses. Claims of quality decline, controversy, or problematic portrayals require specific scope and explanation. Spin-off potential is an editorial hypothesis, not a content fact.

catalog_query_contract.policy: Join authoritative catalog facts and current availability; never ask the descriptive fingerprint to invent them.
entity_resolution: Disney and Pixar can denote companies or brands; resolve intent explicitly.
Star Wars, Marvel, James Bond, and Godzilla queries require franchise or brand identifiers.
Studio Ghibli is an organization query.
Stephen King is a person/source-author query, not a franchise.
Language labels such as Korean, Malayalam, Hindi, Telugu, Tamil, or Japanese do not establish culture or genre.
catalog_query_contract.freshness: Use the existing catalog availability precision and freshness rules. Unknown availability is distinct from a confirmed nonmatching offer.
catalog_query_contract.best: A ranking intent with explicit quality/popularity sources and vote support, not a fingerprint attribute.
catalog_query_contract.reading_demand: Derive per viewer and offer from language proficiency, selected audio/subtitles, visual text, and accessibility version; not a fixed property of the original-language title.

profiles.general_similarity: Evaluate a compact selection of core_candidate traits, normalize group contribution, and compare intensity as well as profile shape.
profiles.content_similarity: Use relevant themes, mechanisms, relationships, and narrative engines; avoid counting the same concept through aliases or parent/child features.
profiles.aesthetic_similarity: Prioritize visual, sonic, action, and storytelling treatment.
profiles.tonight: Combine viewing demands, contextual fit, runtime, personal preferences, and watchability.
profiles.advisory_exclusion: Apply explicit advisory rules with an unknown policy rather than subtracting similarity.

retrieval_contract.weights: No production weights are prescribed by this draft. Fit and evaluate them using judged title pairs and actual query tasks.
retrieval_contract.missingness: Compare jointly assessed features and report evidence coverage. Too little overlap yields insufficient evidence, not a high match.
retrieval_contract.zeros: Shared absence of sparse topics is not positive evidence of content similarity.
retrieval_contract.metric: Do not use cosine alone when absolute intensity matters; evaluate intensity-sensitive distances and separate group scores.
retrieval_contract.hierarchy: Broad themes and narrow concepts may coexist for filtering, but hierarchy membership is not an extra independent similarity vote.
retrieval_contract.negation: Hard exclusions use independently evaluated predicates, not a negative embedding or a positive-score complement.
retrieval_contract.spoilers: Spoiler-sensitive attributes can support private matching but must not appear in explanations, facets, or generated copy without the viewer opting in.
evaluation_tasks: one graphic scene in an otherwise gentle work
Christmas setting versus Christmas viewing association
resolved central conflict with an ambiguous final image
a show whose seasons substantially change
less-known or international titles with incomplete evidence

query_examples.unknown_policy: Unknown age/content suitability is not verified suitable.

advisory_rule.acceptable: Verified absent or assessed explicitness at most 2, under the viewer-defined tolerance.
advisory_rule.unknown_policy: Exclude unknown or inadequately covered assessments from the strict result set.

query_examples.ranking: Action and aesthetic similarity with intensity-sensitive comparison.

query_examples.explanation_policy: Use ending attributes privately; suppress specific ending details without spoiler opt-in.

catalog_filters.offer_video_resolution: 2160p for the matching offer in the viewer country

query_examples.ranking: Explicit quality source and vote support.
query_examples.fingerprint_requirement: No invented Ghibli, Japanese-culture, or 4K trait.

validation_boundary: JSON Schema validates structure, known attribute names, ranges, statuses, and local enums. A semantic validator must resolve evidence/scope IDs, enforce registry applicability and fact value types, check coverage before advisory absence, and enforce spoiler handling.
